Outside view: the last ten Friday readings sit in a narrow band from -34.3 to -37.3, mean ≈ -36.0, with no durable trend since late June. Week-over-week changes are -0.3, +0.6, +1.4, -1.0, -0.7, -0.7, -0.3, +3.0, -1.5 — median absolute move ~0.7, sd ~1.3 (inflated by the single +3.0 jump on 8/21, which promptly gave back half). Because MRP smoothing makes moves persistent but small, a naive extrapolation from the last value (-35.8) with modest pull toward the ten-week mean (-36.0) lands near -35.9.

Inside view: nothing discrete is scheduled between 8/28 and the 9/3 model date. The ambient news flow (record-low approval on prices/inflation, continued backlash to immigration enforcement, CNN/SSRS and UnidosUS showing Hispanic men deeply negative) all points mildly downward rather than upward, but these are slow-moving pressures already priced into a series that has been range-bound for two months. Worth about -0.2. Labor Day timing can thin panel intake slightly, which mostly just makes the estimate stickier — no directional effect. Net: -36.0.

Pre-mortem: the most likely way I'm badly wrong is a repeat of the 8/21-type jolt — a 3-point single-week swing in the subgroup, which happens roughly once in ten weeks here (Hispanic cell is one of the thinner cells, so occasional model-revision-driven step changes occur, in either direction, and nightly revisions can also restate the recent path). Second failure mode: a genuine floor effect — disapproval near 72% leaves less room to fall, so extreme downside beyond about -39 is unlikely. Correction: keep the mean essentially at the recent level and fatten the sd beyond the median move to cover step-change weeks, while not assuming direction.

Calibrate: sd of 1.3 puts ~two-thirds of outcomes in roughly [-37.3, -34.7], which matches the observed band of the last ten releases and admits the occasional 2-3 point jolt at the tails.
